concepts.title: Composition of functions
concepts.description: For f:A→B and g:B→C, the composite g∘f:A→C sends x to g(f(x)).

concepts.title: Intersection of a family of sets
concepts.description: Inside a specified ambient set, the elements belonging to every member of the family.

concepts.title: Least upper bound in a partially ordered set
concepts.description: For A⊆P, its least upper bound is an upper bound s satisfying s≤b for every upper bound b of A, when such an s exists.

concepts.title: Natural number
concepts.description: One of 0, 1, 2, …; natural numbers count finite collections.

concepts.title: Ordered pair
concepts.description: A pair (x,y) with distinguished first and second entries; (x,y)=(x′,y′) exactly when x=x′ and y=y′.

concepts.title: Partial order
concepts.description: A reflexive, antisymmetric and transitive binary relation, usually written ≤.

concepts.title: Preimage of a subset under a function
Sequence in a set
concepts.description: A function from the natural numbers, or the positive natural numbers, to that set.

concepts.title: Set
concepts.description: A collection of distinct elements, regarded as one object.

concepts.title: Complement of a subset
concepts.description: For A⊆Ω, its complement Ω∖A consists of the elements of Ω that do not belong to A.

concepts.title: Subset
concepts.description: A⊆B means every element of A is an element of B.

concepts.title: Total order
concepts.description: A partial order in which any two elements are comparable.

concepts.title: Union of a family of sets
concepts.description: The set of elements belonging to at least one member of the family.

concepts.title: Derivative of a real function
concepts.description: The derivative f′(x) is the finite limit of (f(x+h)−f(x))/h as h→0, when it exists. Higher derivatives are defined by iteration.

concepts.title: Factorial domination of fixed exponentials
concepts.description: For every fixed real C>0, the sequence Cⁿ/n! tends to zero.

concepts.title: Finite set
concepts.description: A set X is finite if it is bijective with {1,…,n} for some natural number n≥0; its cardinality is n.
